name: Floral lavender
lede: Floral lavender is a brighter, more saturated purple than the muted [[lavender]] of the flower it is named for, and our painting archive has no record of it at all.

sections.title: Brighter than the plant
sections.body:
Lavender, the plant, gives its name to one of the oldest flower-derived color words in English, but Floral lavender pushes well past the grayed, dusty purple of the real [[flower:lavender|lavender]] bloom toward a brighter, more saturated hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[light-hortense-violet]] and [[orchid-purple]], at 
Wikipedia is our only source for this particular name and hex value; no older dictionary, plate or survey in our library carries it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive shows this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of it, as photographed [3]. A bright, modern-saturation purple like this is simply absent from the pigments and dyes historical painters had on hand [3]. Measured in LCH it comes out at lightness 62, chroma 80, hue 314 degrees, than to any grayer lavender [2].
